{{Short description|American biologist (1940–2024)}}
{{for|the Canadian conservationist and senator|Diane Griffin (conservationist)}}
'''Diane Edmund Griffin''' (May 5, 1940 – October 28, 2024) was an American biologist who was the university distinguished professor and a professor in the Department of Molecular Microbiology and Immunology at the [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]], where she was the department chair from 1994 to 2015. Until her death, Griffin served as the {{when|date=April 2022}} vice-president of the National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Zagorski | first1 = N. | title = Profile of Diane E. Griffin| doi = 10.1073/pnas.0505531102 | journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | volume = 102 | issue = 33 | pages = 11578–11580 | year = 2005 | pmid = 16087864 | pmc =1188013 | bibcode = 2005PNAS..10211578Z | doi-access = free }}</ref> She held joint appointments in the departments of Neurology and Medicine. In 2004, Griffin was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS) in the discipline of [[List of members of the National Academy of Sciences (Microbial biology)|microbial biology]].<ref name=FacultyPage>{{Cite web |url=http://faculty.jhsph.edu/Default.cfm?faculty_id=281 |title=Bloomberg School of Public Health faculty webpage |access-date=2009-08-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090722004001/http://faculty.jhsph.edu/Default.cfm?faculty_id=281 |archive-date=2009-07-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Background==
Griffin was born on May 5, 1940.<ref>{{cite web | first= Stephanie | last= Berger | title= Diane E. Griffin M.D., Ph.D. | work= Archives of Maryland | publisher= Maryland State Archives | url= http://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/015100/015134/html/15134bio.html | access-date= 2013-04-08 | archive-date= 2017-04-24 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170424090308/http://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/015100/015134/html/15134bio.html | url-status= live }}</ref> After earning her undergraduate degree from [[Augustana College (Illinois)|Augustana College]] in [[Rock Island, Illinois]], she joined a joint MD/PhD graduate program at [[Stanford University]], where she pursued research on [[immunoglobulin]]s. Griffin received her PhD and MD in 1968 and remained at [[Stanford Hospital]] for her [[Internship (medicine)|internship]] and [[Residency (medicine)|residency]].<ref name=ISNVPioneer/>

Griffin performed postdoctoral research in virology at the [[Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine]]. Along with [[Janice E. Clements]] and others, Griffin is a notable trainee of neurovirology specialist [[Richard T. Johnson]].<ref name=ISNVPioneer>{{Cite web |url=http://www.isnv.org/pioneer/pioneer09.php |title=2009 recipient of the ISNV Pioneer in NeuroVirology Award |access-date=2013-06-29 |archive-date=2017-04-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170429051336/http://isnv.org/pioneer/pioneer09.php |url-status=live }}</ref>

Griffin died on October 28, 2024, at the age of 84.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: Diane Edmund Griffin, MD, PhD, 1940–2024 |url=https://publichealth.jhu.edu/2024/in-memoriam-diane-edmund-griffin-md-phd-1940-2024 |website=Johns Hopkins University |access-date=2 December 2024}}</ref>

==Career==
Griffin became a faculty member at Johns Hopkins in 1973 in the Department of Neurology. She attained the rank of full professor in 1986. In 1994, Griffin became the chair of the Department of Molecular Microbiology and Immunology at the [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|Johns Hopkins School of Hygiene and Public Health]], now known as the Bloomberg School of Public Health.<ref name=ISNVPioneer/> She held the chair position from 1994 to 2014, as well as numerous other roles science leadership in academic and government organizations, including Vice President of the National Academy of Sciences from 2013 to 2024.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Casadevall |first=Arturo |last2=Hardwick |first2=J. Marie |date=2025-04-30 |title=Diane E. Griffin, physician–scientist extraordinaire |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q134379799 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=122 |issue=18 |doi=10.1073/PNAS.2424274122|doi-access=free |pmc=12067231 }}</ref>

==Research==
{{Scholia}}
[[Virology]] was Griffin's specialty from the time of her postdoctoral work. Her research examined how the body responds to viral infection. Griffin placed particular emphasis on the [[central nervous system]], researching the effects of [[Sindbis virus]] and the [[measles]] virus on the brain.<ref name=ISNVPioneer/> Further, her work contributed to knowledge of how long-term immunity to re-infection with measles develops.<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Academy of Sciences Member Directory|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/diane-e-griffin-tcuybl/|access-date=May 22, 2020|archive-date=July 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180720183326/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/3007695.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Griffin has received numerous awards and honorific memberships.
*Membership in the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2004)
*Membership of the [[American Academy of Microbiology]]
*Membership in the [[National Academy of Medicine]]<ref name=FacultyPage/>
*Membership in the [[American Philosophical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Diane+E.+Griffin&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-08-05|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-05-01|title=Daniels, Griffin elected to American Philosophical Society|url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2018/05/01/daniels-griffin-american-philosophical-society/|access-date=2021-08-05|website=The Hub|language=en}}</ref>
*Inducted into the [[Maryland Women's Hall of Fame]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Diane E. Griffin, Maryland Women's Hall of Fame|url=https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/educ/exhibits/womenshall/html/griffin.html|access-date=2021-08-05|website=msa.maryland.gov|archive-date=2021-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805183349/https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/educ/exhibits/womenshall/html/griffin.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
*Awarded the [[Rudolf Virchow]] Medal, [[University of Würzburg]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Virchow Medal - Universität Würzburg|url=https://www.uni-wuerzburg.de/en/rvz/rudolf-virchow-center/in-retrospect/virchow-medal/|access-date=2021-08-05|website=www.uni-wuerzburg.de|archive-date=2021-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805183350/https://www.uni-wuerzburg.de/en/rvz/rudolf-virchow-center/in-retrospect/virchow-medal/|url-status=live}}</ref>
*Awarded the Wallace Sterling Lifetime Alumni Achievement Award, [[Stanford University]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sterling Award|url=https://www.med.stanford.edu/content/sm/alumni/events/sterling-award.html|access-date=2021-08-05|website=Alumni Association|language=sm|archive-date=2021-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805183355/https://www.med.stanford.edu/content/sm/alumni/events/sterling-award.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
*Awarded the Pioneer in NeuroVirology Award by the [[International Society for NeuroVirology]] at the 9th International Symposium on NeuroVirology held in Miami, Florida, in 2009.<ref name="ISNVPioneer" />
